The plan is `notes/plan-618-daily-integral.md`.

## Running this yourself

Everything below is R; no shell needed. The analysis needs plant built from this branch, against the exact versions of phylloptim and odelia it pins (`== 0.26.2` and `== 0.10.5`). They are installed into a private library folder, `Rlib-618`, beside this file, so nothing in your system or user R library changes. You need a C++20 compiler (Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS, Rtools on Windows) and, to render, Quarto.

**1. Get this file**, if you do not have it yet, from any R session:

```r
dir.create("onepoint-618", showWarnings = FALSE)
download.file(paste0("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/traitecoevo/plant/",
                     "experiment/618-daily-integral/notes/618-daily-integral/analysis.qmd"),
              file.path("onepoint-618", "analysis.qmd"))
```

**2. Open it and run all chunks**, with the working directory set to this file's folder (RStudio does that for a `.qmd`; elsewhere `setwd()` to it). The first chunk below installs the three packages into `Rlib-618` if they are not already there (once; a few minutes of compiling), and every later chunk loads them from there. Or render the whole thing from R:

```r
quarto::quarto_render("analysis.qmd")   # needs the quarto R package and Quarto itself
```

Runs are cached as `.rds` beside this file; delete them to rerun. A cold run takes about an hour, nearly all of it the diurnal reference arm D. To try your own site, add an entry to `sites` in the helpers chunk.

```{r install}
#| code-fold: false
## The private library, beside this file. Put first on the search path for
## this R session only: the system and user libraries are never written to.
## Created before it is normalised: normalizePath() leaves a path that does not
## exist yet as it was given.
dir.create("Rlib-618", showWarnings = FALSE)
lib <- normalizePath("Rlib-618")
.libPaths(c(lib, setdiff(.libPaths(), lib)))

installed_ok <- function() {
  ok <- function(pkg, version = NULL) {
    d <- file.path(lib, pkg, "DESCRIPTION")
    file.exists(d) && (is.null(version) || read.dcf(d, "Version")[1] == version)
  }
  ok("odelia", "0.10.5") && ok("phylloptim", "0.26.2") && ok("plant") &&
    "one_point_c_assimilation_slope" %in%
      names(get("control", asNamespace("plant"))())
}
if (!isTRUE(tryCatch(installed_ok(), error = function(e) FALSE))) {
  if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("remotes", lib = lib)
  ## Pinned upstreams first, then plant. upgrade = "never" stops remotes from
  ## replacing them with newer releases; missing CRAN dependencies (Rcpp, BH,
  ## ...) also go into `lib`.
  remotes::install_github("traitecoevo/odelia@v0.10.5", lib = lib, upgrade = "never")
  remotes::install_github("traitecoevo/phylloptim@v0.26.2", lib = lib, upgrade = "never")
  remotes::install_github("traitecoevo/plant@experiment/618-daily-integral",
                          lib = lib, upgrade = "never", force = TRUE)
}
## Where each came from: all three should be inside `lib`.
sapply(c("plant", "phylloptim", "odelia"), find.package)
```

If plant was already loaded in this R session from another library, restart R before running the chunks, or the old one stays in use (the setup chunk checks and stops). The plotting packages this file uses (ggplot2, dplyr, tidyr, knitr) can come from your normal library; if any are missing, `install.packages(..., lib = lib)`.

## The question

TF24 turns one leaf solve into a year's carbon and water by multiplying by a fixed twelve-hour day. Towers et al. (in prep., "CODA") argue that one solve at solar noon, times the photoperiod, times a calibration constant c, recovers the daily integral well enough for stand models. Here we test that inside plant, against cheap alternatives: the same stand under the same forcing, integrated six ways.

| Arm | `control$daily_integration` | What a rate evaluation does | Solves |
|---|---|---|---|
| **D** (reference) | `"diurnal"`, 48 points | midpoint rule over the photoperiod | 48 |
| **L** | `"lobatto"` | 5-point Gauss–Lobatto; the dark sunrise and sunset nodes are −R_d and no water, so need no solve | 3 |
| **Ol** | `"one-point"`, c(I) | noon × photoperiod × c, with c = a + b·log(I/500) of the crown's intercepted noon PPFD I | 1 |
| **Oc** | `"one-point"`, c = c̄ | noon × photoperiod × one constant c (the paper's simplest calibration) | 1 |
| **O1** | `"one-point"`, c = 1 | noon × photoperiod, uncalibrated | 1 |
| **F** | `""` (default) | one solve × 12 h, the model as it runs today | 1 |

Every arm sees the same noon drivers; they differ only in how the day is integrated. Carbon and water have separate constants in Oc and Ol.

## What we found

Two synthetic sites, written 2026-11-03 (numbers from the tables below):

- **Gauss–Lobatto (L) is the method to use.** Three solves a day and no calibration. At the leaf its daily carbon is within 1.4% (temperate) and 2.8% (arid) RMS of the 96-point integral. In 10-year stands it is within ~2% of the reference on LAI, biomass, water use and the tallest cohort. In 50-year patches its resident fitness is +6% from the reference at the temperate site. It costs 3.4–3.8× the one-point method and 1/15 of the reference: about 10 s against 3 s and 140 s for a 10-year stand.
- **Light-dependent c (Ol) is the best one-solve method, but not good enough for fitness.** c is one function of the leaf's intercepted noon PPFD, linear in its log, and the same at both sites (slope 0.158 for carbon at each). At the leaf it is within 4.5–5.5% RMS. It gets stand totals and the tallest cohort nearly right at 10 years (within 2% temperate, 7% arid), but over-feeds the understorey (31–71% more plants above 1 m). The reason is visible in the calibration figure: below about 80 µmol/m2/s the true ratio falls away from the log-linear line (about 0.19 against the line's 0.4 near 50), so the deepest shade is over-credited. Its 50-year fitness is −66% from the reference.
- **A constant c (Oc) fixes the stand's totals only as well as its training sample matches the stand.** Calibrated on full sun to 20% openness, it matched 10-year biomass (−3% temperate, +7% arid). Calibrated on full sun to 5% openness, as here, it misses by −25%. Either way it distorts size structure (up to 14× the plants above 1 m, the tallest cohort 34–40% short), and its 50-year fitness is essentially zero against the reference's 0.015.
- **Today's TF24 (F) overstates the day by 25–40%,** nearly doubling temperate biomass at 10 years and multiplying 50-year fitness 180-fold. Any calibration matters more than no calibration; the shape of the day matters more than any calibration.
- **Why size structure is the sensitive output.** The day-to-noon ratio falls from about 0.85 in full sun to 0.25 in deep shade. Any method that does not see the shape of each cohort's day credits shaded and sunlit cohorts differently from the reference, and competition between sizes is built on exactly that difference. Fitness amplifies it further, because reproduction waits on reaching a size.

## Helpers

```{r helpers}
## ---- sites ------------------------------------------------------------------
sites <- list(
  temperate = list(name = "temperate", latitude = -33.6, tau = 0.7,
                   vpd_mean = 1.3, vpd_seasonal = 0.5, vpd_diurnal_amp = 0.4,
                   rain_mean = 0.9, rain_seasonal = 0.3),
  arid = list(name = "arid", latitude = -22.3, tau = 0.8,
              vpd_mean = 2.1, vpd_seasonal = 0.5, vpd_diurnal_amp = 0.35,
              rain_mean = 0.3, rain_seasonal = 0.8))
vpd_peak_hour <- 14.5
summer_peak <- 0.04   # years after 1 January: mid-January
es_25 <- 0.6108 * exp(17.27 * 25 / (25 + 237.3))   # kPa, saturation at the pinned 25 C
umol_par_per_joule <- 4.57                          # phylloptim's constant

vpd_shape <- function(hour, amp, peak = vpd_peak_hour)
  1 + amp * cos(2 * pi * (hour - peak) / 24)

site_drivers <- function(site, years, knots_per_year = 48) {
  t <- seq(0, years + 1, by = 1 / knots_per_year)
  sun <- plant:::tf24_solar_day(t, site$latitude)
  s <- sun$sin_elevation_noon
  season <- cos(2 * pi * (t - summer_peak))
  d <- data.frame(time = t, daylength = sun$daylength,
                  SWdown = 1360 * site$tau^(1 / s) * s,
                  atm_vpd = site$vpd_mean + site$vpd_seasonal * season,
                  rainfall = site$rain_mean * (1 + site$rain_seasonal * season))
  ## The day's VPD peak must stay below saturation at the pinned leaf
  ## temperature, or the leaf refuses the solve.
  peak <- max(d$atm_vpd) * (1 + site$vpd_diurnal_amp) /
    vpd_shape(12, site$vpd_diurnal_amp)
  stopifnot(peak < 0.95 * es_25)
  d
}

site_env <- function(site, years) {
  d <- site_drivers(site, years)
  env <- Environment("TF24")
  for (v in c("SWdown", "atm_vpd", "rainfall")) {
    env$extrinsic_drivers_set_variable(v, d$time, d[[v]])
  }
  env$extrinsic_drivers_set_constant("atm_vpd_diurnal_amp", site$vpd_diurnal_amp)
  env$latitude <- site$latitude
  env$vpd_peak_hour <- vpd_peak_hour
  env
}

## ---- stands and arms --------------------------------------------------------
lma <- 0.1978791        # TF24 hyperpar's central lma
birth_rate <- 20

## The default schedule is dense early and years apart late; adding a regular
## grid keeps the early cohorts and gives a regular census (run_to stops only at
## introductions). Every arm runs on the same schedule.
stand_parameters <- function(years, grid_dt = 1 / 12, patch_type = "fixed") {
  p <- scm_base_parameters("TF24")
  p$max_patch_lifetime <- years
  p$patch_type <- patch_type
  p <- add_strategies(p, trait_matrix(lma, "lma"), hyperpar = TF24_hyperpar,
                      birth_rate = list(birth_rate))
  sched <- p$node_schedule_times[[1]]
  p$node_schedule_times[[1]] <-
    sort(unique(c(sched, seq(0, years - grid_dt, by = grid_dt))))
  p
}

arm_control <- function(arm, cal = NULL, n = 48L) {
  switch(arm,
    F  = control(),
    O1 = control(daily_integration = "one-point"),
    Oc = control(daily_integration = "one-point",
                 one_point_c_assimilation = cal$c_hat[["A"]],
                 one_point_c_transpiration = cal$c_hat[["E"]]),
    Ol = control(daily_integration = "one-point",
                 one_point_c_assimilation = cal$c_light[["A"]],
                 one_point_c_assimilation_slope = cal$c_light[["A_slope"]],
                 one_point_c_transpiration = cal$c_light[["E"]],
                 one_point_c_transpiration_slope = cal$c_light[["E_slope"]],
                 one_point_c_light_min = cal$c_light[["I_min"]],
                 one_point_c_light_max = cal$c_light[["I_max"]]),
    L  = control(daily_integration = "lobatto"),
    D  = control(daily_integration = "diurnal", daily_integration_points = n),
    stop("unknown arm ", arm))
}

## One stand, advanced a census interval at a time with run_to(). Records the
## stand census, the soil, and every node's height (keyed by its introduction
## time) so growth can be differenced along cohorts.
run_arm <- function(site, arm, cal = NULL, years = 10, census_dt = 1 / 12,
                    patch_type = "fixed", n = 48L) {
  p <- stand_parameters(years, census_dt, patch_type)
  scm <- run_scm(p, site_env(site, years), arm_control(arm, cal, n), run = FALSE)
  times <- seq(census_dt, years, length.out = round(years / census_dt))
  census <- vector("list", length(times))
  nodes <- vector("list", length(times))
  elapsed <- system.time({
    for (i in seq_along(times)) {
      scm$run_to(times[i])
      env <- scm$patch$environment
      sp <- scm$patch$species[[1]]
      flux <- env$get_soil_water_state_cumulative_flux()
      census[[i]] <- data.frame(time = scm$time, t(stand_census(scm)),
                                theta = mean(env$get_soil_water_state()),
                                uptake = flux[[4]])
      nodes[[i]] <- data.frame(time = scm$time, birth = sp$node_times,
                               height = sp$heights,
                               log_density = sp$log_densities)
    }
    if (!scm$complete) scm$run()
  })[["elapsed"]]
  counts <- plant:::census_operating_point_counts_tf24(scm)
  list(site = site$name, arm = arm,
       census = do.call(rbind, census), nodes = do.call(rbind, nodes),
       offspring = scm$offspring_production, fitness = scm$net_reproduction_ratios,
       elapsed = elapsed, solves = sum(unlist(counts)), steps = length(scm$ode_times),
       density_in_birth_date = scm$patch$species[[1]]$density_in_birth_date)
}

## ---- calibrating c ----------------------------------------------------------
## A training sample of individual TF24 leaves evaluated through plant's own
## code path. Rates are daylight means, so each is multiplied by its day's
## photoperiod; I is the crown's intercepted noon PPFD, as the C++ computes it.
calibration_sample <- function(site, theta, n_days = 100, heights = c(1, 4, 12),
                               openness = c(1, 0.5, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05), seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  expand.grid(day = runif(n_days), height = heights, openness = openness,
              theta = theta)
}

day_rates <- function(site, sample, method, n = 48L) {
  s <- stand_parameters(1)$strategies[[1]]
  s$control$daily_integration <- method
  s$control$daily_integration_points <- as.integer(n)
  env <- site_env(site, 1)
  ind <- TF24_Individual(s)
  nl <- env$get_soil_number_of_depths()
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(sample), 2, dimnames = list(NULL, c("profit", "transpiration")))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(sample))) {
    env$time <- sample$day[i]
    env$set_fixed_environment(sample$openness[i], height_max = 150)
    env$set_soil_water_state(rep(sample$theta[i], nl))
    ind$set_state("height", sample$height[i])
    ind$compute_rates(env)
    out[i, ] <- c(ind$aux("profit"), ind$aux("transpiration"))
  }
  daylength <- plant:::tf24_solar_day(sample$day, site$latitude)$daylength
  SWdown <- env$extrinsic_drivers_evaluate_range("SWdown", sample$day)
  data.frame(sample, daylength = daylength,
             I = s$pars$k_I * pmax(sample$openness, 1e-4) *
               umol_par_per_joule * env$f_PAR * SWdown,
             P = out[, "profit"] * daylength, T = out[, "transpiration"] * daylength)
}

## Constant c: ratio of sums, sum(P*) / sum(P1). Light-dependent c: the least
## squares fit of P* = P1 (a + b log(I/500)) over the same sample, held flat
## outside the sample's range of I.
calibrate_c <- function(site, theta, ...) {
  smp <- calibration_sample(site, theta, ...)
  one <- day_rates(site, smp, "one-point")
  d48 <- day_rates(site, smp, "diurnal", 48L)
  x <- log(one$I / 500)
  fA <- lm(d48$P ~ 0 + one$P + I(one$P * x))
  fE <- lm(d48$T ~ 0 + one$T + I(one$T * x))
  list(c_hat = c(A = sum(d48$P) / sum(one$P), E = sum(d48$T) / sum(one$T)),
       c_light = c(A = coef(fA)[[1]], A_slope = coef(fA)[[2]],
                   E = coef(fE)[[1]], E_slope = coef(fE)[[2]],
                   I_min = min(one$I), I_max = max(one$I)),
       one = one, d48 = d48)
}

c_of_light <- function(cal, I, which = "A") {
  cl <- cal$c_light
  x <- log(pmin(pmax(I, cl[["I_min"]]), cl[["I_max"]]) / 500)
  cl[[which]] + cl[[paste0(which, "_slope")]] * x
}
```

## Two synthetic sites

Illustrative climates, not cited climatologies: a **temperate** site at the latitude of Cumberland Plain (−33.6°, the paper's base site) and an **arid** one at Alice Springs Mulga's (−22.3°). Noon shortwave is clear-sky geometry times a transmissivity; noon VPD and rainfall are seasonal cosines peaking in mid-January. Through the day, shortwave follows sin(solar elevation) and VPD one cosine harmonic peaking at 14:30. Because plant pins leaf temperature at 25 °C and the leaf refuses VPD at or above saturation, the day's VPD peak is held below 0.95·e_s(25 °C) ≈ 3.0 kPa: the arid site is as dry as that pin allows.

```{r fig-drivers}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Noon drivers and photoperiod over one year at the two sites."
drv <- bind_rows(lapply(names(sites), function(nm)
  site_drivers(sites[[nm]], 1) |> mutate(site = nm))) |>
  filter(time <= 1) |>
  transmute(site, time,
            `Noon shortwave (W/m2)` = SWdown, `Noon VPD (kPa)` = atm_vpd,
            `Rainfall (m/yr)` = rainfall, `Photoperiod (h)` = daylength) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(site, time))
ggplot(drv, aes(time, value, colour = site)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = site_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Time of year (years from 1 January)", y = NULL)
```

## Calibrating c, and a day's integral at the leaf

The training sample is 100 random days × plant heights {1, 4, 12 m} × canopy openness {1, 0.5, 0.2, 0.1, 0.05} × three soil-water levels (the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles of that site's soil water in arm F), per site. The constant c̄ is a ratio of sums, ΣP\*/ΣP⁽¹⁾ (a mean of ratios blows up wherever noon profit is near zero). The light-dependent c is the least-squares fit of P\* = P⁽¹⁾·(a + b·log(I/500)) on the same sample.

```{r runs}
base <- cached("arms_base.rds", lapply(sites, function(site)
  list(F = run_arm(site, "F"), O1 = run_arm(site, "O1"), D = run_arm(site, "D"))))
cal <- cached("cal.rds", lapply(sites, function(site) {
  theta <- unname(quantile(base[[site$name]]$F$census$theta, c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9)))
  calibrate_c(site, theta)
}))
extra <- cached("arms_cal.rds", lapply(sites, function(site) {
  cl <- cal[[site$name]]
  list(Oc = run_arm(site, "Oc", cl), Ol = run_arm(site, "Ol", cl),
       L = run_arm(site, "L"))
}))
arms <- lapply(setNames(names(sites), names(sites)), function(nm)
  c(base[[nm]], extra[[nm]], list(cal = cal[[nm]])))

c_tab <- bind_rows(lapply(names(cal), function(nm) {
  cl <- cal[[nm]]
  data.frame(site = nm, c_A = cl$c_hat[["A"]], c_E = cl$c_hat[["E"]],
             a_A = cl$c_light[["A"]], b_A = cl$c_light[["A_slope"]],
             a_E = cl$c_light[["E"]], b_E = cl$c_light[["E_slope"]],
             I_range = sprintf("%.0f-%.0f", cl$c_light[["I_min"]], cl$c_light[["I_max"]]))
}))
knitr::kable(c_tab, digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Site", "c̄ carbon", "c̄ water", "a carbon", "b carbon",
                "a water", "b water", "I range (µmol/m2/s)"),
  caption = "Calibration constants. Constant c (Oc), and c(I) = a + b log(I/500) (Ol).")
```

```{r fig-c-light}
#| fig-height: 3.6
#| fig-cap: "c is a function of the leaf's light, and the same function at both sites. Points: the diurnal integral over noon × photoperiod, summed within bins of intercepted noon PPFD (bins whose noon profit is under 5% of the largest are left out: the ratio is meaningless there). Solid: the fitted c(I) for each site. Dashed: the site's constant c̄."
binned <- bind_rows(lapply(names(cal), function(nm) {
  one <- cal[[nm]]$one; d <- cal[[nm]]$d48
  b <- cut(log(one$I), 10)
  noon <- tapply(one$P, b, mean)
  data.frame(site = nm, I = as.vector(exp(tapply(log(one$I), b, mean))),
             carbon = as.vector(tapply(d$P, b, sum) / tapply(one$P, b, sum)),
             water = as.vector(tapply(d$T, b, sum) / tapply(one$T, b, sum)),
             keep = as.vector(noon > 0.05 * max(noon)))
})) |> filter(keep) |> select(-keep) |> pivot_longer(c(carbon, water))
fits <- bind_rows(lapply(names(cal), function(nm) {
  cl <- cal[[nm]]; I <- exp(seq(log(cl$c_light[["I_min"]]), log(cl$c_light[["I_max"]]), length.out = 50))
  data.frame(site = nm, I = I, carbon = c_of_light(cl, I, "A"), water = c_of_light(cl, I, "E"))
})) |> pivot_longer(c(carbon, water))
consts <- c_tab |> select(site, carbon = c_A, water = c_E) |> pivot_longer(-site)
ggplot(binned, aes(I, value, colour = site)) +
  geom_line(data = fits, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  geom_hline(data = consts, aes(yintercept = value, colour = site),
             linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~name) + scale_x_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = site_cols, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Intercepted PPFD at noon (µmol/m2/s, log scale)",
       y = "Diurnal / (noon × photoperiod)")
```

```{r form-of-c}
## The form: c linear in log(I), against linear in I, on the per-sample ratio.
form <- bind_rows(lapply(names(cal), function(nm) {
  one <- cal[[nm]]$one; d <- cal[[nm]]$d48
  r <- d$P / one$P; ok <- one$P > 0.05 * max(one$P)
  data.frame(site = nm,
             `R² linear in log I` = summary(lm(r[ok] ~ log(one$I[ok])))$r.squared,
             `R² linear in I` = summary(lm(r[ok] ~ one$I[ok]))$r.squared,
             check.names = FALSE)
}))
knitr::kable(form, digits = 3, caption = "How well each form of c(I) explains the per-sample ratio for carbon (samples whose noon profit is at least 5% of the largest).")
```

Every method can also be checked at the leaf, day by day, before any stand is run. The reference here is the diurnal integral at 96 points.

```{r leaf-accuracy}
leaf_err <- bind_rows(lapply(names(cal), function(nm) {
  cl <- cal[[nm]]; one <- cl$one; d48 <- cl$d48
  smp <- one[, c("day", "height", "openness", "theta")]
  d96 <- cached(sprintf("leaf96_%s.rds", nm), day_rates(sites[[nm]], smp, "diurnal", 96L))
  d24 <- cached(sprintf("leaf24_%s.rds", nm), day_rates(sites[[nm]], smp, "diurnal", 24L))
  lob <- cached(sprintf("leafL_%s.rds", nm), day_rates(sites[[nm]], smp, "lobatto"))
  est <- list(
    `D, 48 solves` = d48$P, `diurnal, 24 solves` = d24$P, `L, 3 solves` = lob$P,
    `Ol, 1 solve` = one$P * c_of_light(cl, one$I, "A"),
    `Oc, 1 solve` = one$P * cl$c_hat[["A"]], `O1, 1 solve` = one$P)
  ## Relative to the day's own magnitude; days whose integral is near zero
  ## would otherwise dominate.
  ok <- abs(d96$P) > 0.05 * max(abs(d96$P))
  bind_rows(lapply(names(est), function(m) {
    e <- est[[m]][ok] / d96$P[ok] - 1
    data.frame(site = nm, method = m, total = sum(est[[m]]) / sum(d96$P) - 1,
               bias = mean(e), rmse = sqrt(mean(e^2)), worst = max(abs(e)))
  }))
}))
leaf_err |>
  mutate(across(c(total, bias, rmse, worst), ~ sprintf("%+.2f%%", 100 * .x))) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Site", "Method", "Error in summed carbon",
                             "Mean daily error", "RMS daily error", "Worst day"),
               caption = "Leaf-level daily carbon against the 96-point diurnal integral, over the calibration sample. Ol and Oc are scored on the sample they were fitted to.")
```

## Ten-year stands

One species at the TF24 hyperparameter defaults (lma `r lma`), seed rain `r birth_rate` per m² per year, a fixed patch for 10 years. The cohort schedule is plant's default plus a monthly grid, the same in every arm, and the stand is censused monthly with plant's own `stand_census()`.

```{r stand-series}
series_of <- function(arms, arm_set) bind_rows(lapply(names(arms), function(nm)
  bind_rows(lapply(arm_set, function(a)
    arms[[nm]][[a]]$census |> mutate(site = nm, arm = a, i = row_number())))))
series <- series_of(arms, arms_all)
series$arm <- factor(series$arm, levels = arms_all)

plot_stand <- function(series, arm_set = arms_plot) {
  long <- series |> filter(arm %in% arm_set) |>
    transmute(site, arm, time,
              `LAI (m2/m2)` = leaf_area, `Above-ground mass (kg/m2)` = mass_above_ground,
              `Soil water (m3/m3)` = theta, `Cumulative uptake (m)` = uptake) |>
    pivot_longer(-c(site, arm, time)) |>
    mutate(name = factor(name, levels = unique(name)),
           site = factor(site, levels = names(sites)),
           arm = factor(arm, levels = arm_set))
  ggplot(long, aes(time, value, colour = arm, linetype = arm)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
    facet_grid(name ~ site, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
    scale_arm + labs(x = "Years", y = NULL) +
    theme(strip.placement = "outside")
}
```

```{r fig-stand}
#| fig-height: 7.5
#| fig-cap: "Ten-year stand trajectories. Rows: leaf area index, above-ground biomass, layer-mean soil water, cumulative transpiration."
plot_stand(series)
```

### Size structure and growth

Density is carried per unit birth date (TF24's default coordinate), so the size distribution is shown as the number of plants at least a given height: the density integrated over birth date from the oldest cohort down, which needs no change of coordinate.

```{r sizes}
at_time <- function(nodes, t) {
  tt <- unique(nodes$time); nodes[nodes$time == tt[which.min(abs(tt - t))], ]
}
taller_than <- function(n) {
  n <- n[order(n$birth), ]; dens <- exp(n$log_density)
  n$N_taller <- c(0, cumsum(0.5 * (head(dens, -1) + tail(dens, -1)) * diff(n$birth)))
  n
}
sizes_of <- function(arms, arm_set, years) bind_rows(lapply(names(arms), function(nm)
  bind_rows(lapply(arm_set, function(a)
    bind_rows(lapply(years, function(t)
      taller_than(at_time(arms[[nm]][[a]]$nodes, t)) |>
        mutate(site = nm, arm = a, year = t)))))))
plot_sizes <- function(sizes, years, arm_set = arms_plot) {
  d <- sizes |> filter(arm %in% arm_set, N_taller > 1e-3) |>
    mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arm_set), site = factor(site, levels = names(sites)),
           year = factor(paste("Year", year), levels = paste("Year", years)))
  ggplot(d, aes(height, N_taller, colour = arm, linetype = arm)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
    facet_grid(site ~ year, scales = "free") +
    scale_y_log10() + scale_arm +
    labs(x = "Height (m)", y = "Plants at least this tall (per m2)")
}
sizes <- sizes_of(arms, arms_all, c(2, 5, 10))
```

```{r fig-sizes}
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-cap: "Plants per m² at least a given height, at years 2, 5 and 10."
plot_sizes(sizes, c(2, 5, 10))
```

```{r fig-growth}
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-cap: "Height growth rate of each cohort against its height, over the month ending at years 2, 5 and 10."
growth <- bind_rows(lapply(names(arms), function(nm)
  bind_rows(lapply(arms_plot, function(a) {
    nd <- arms[[nm]][[a]]$nodes; tt <- unique(nd$time)
    bind_rows(lapply(c(2, 5, 10), function(t) {
      k <- which.min(abs(tt - t))
      b <- nd[nd$time == tt[k], ]; e <- nd[nd$time == tt[k - 1], ]
      inner_join(e, b, by = "birth", suffix = c("0", "1")) |>
        transmute(height = height0, dHdt = (height1 - height0) / (time1 - time0),
                  site = nm, arm = a, year = t)
    }))
  })))) |>
  mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arms_plot), site = factor(site, levels = names(sites)),
         year = factor(paste("Year", year), levels = paste("Year", c(2, 5, 10))))
ggplot(growth, aes(height, dHdt, colour = arm, linetype = arm)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(site ~ year, scales = "free") +
  scale_arm + labs(x = "Height (m)", y = "Height growth (m/yr)")
```

### How far each arm is from the reference

```{r table-outcomes}
outcome_table <- function(series, sizes, final_year, extra = NULL) {
  end <- series |> group_by(site, arm) |> slice_max(i, n = 1) |> ungroup()
  tall <- sizes |> filter(year == final_year) |> group_by(site, arm) |>
    summarise(top_height = max(height[exp(log_density) > 1e-6]),
              N_over_1m = max(N_taller[height >= 1], 0), .groups = "drop")
  lai_dev <- series |> filter(time >= 1) |>
    group_by(site, i) |> mutate(ref = leaf_area[arm == "D"]) |> ungroup() |>
    group_by(site, arm) |> summarise(max_lai_dev = max(abs(leaf_area / ref - 1)), .groups = "drop")
  outc <- end |> select(site, arm, leaf_area, mass_above_ground, uptake) |>
    left_join(tall, by = c("site", "arm")) |> left_join(lai_dev, by = c("site", "arm"))
  if (!is.null(extra)) outc <- left_join(outc, extra, by = c("site", "arm"))
  cols <- intersect(c("leaf_area", "mass_above_ground", "uptake", "top_height",
                      "N_over_1m", "fitness"), names(outc))
  outc |> group_by(site) |>
    mutate(across(all_of(cols), ~ .x / .x[arm == "D"] - 1)) |> ungroup() |>
    filter(arm != "D") |> arrange(site, arm)
}
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%+.0f%%", 100 * x)
rel10 <- outcome_table(series, sizes, 10)
rel10 |>
  transmute(Site = site, Arm = arm, `LAI` = pct(leaf_area),
            `Above-ground mass` = pct(mass_above_ground), `Cumulative uptake` = pct(uptake),
            `Tallest cohort` = pct(top_height), `Plants > 1 m` = pct(N_over_1m),
            `Worst LAI, yr 1-10` = pct(max_lai_dev)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Difference from D at year 10 (last column: largest |relative LAI difference| over years 1-10).")
```

Offspring production is not compared at 10 years: these stands have barely begun reproducing, so it measures the onset of reproduction, not reproductive output. The 50-year patches below take that up.

## Speed

```{r timing}
## One plain run_scm() per arm -- no census loop -- timing the run and
## counting leaf solves by the operating point each ended on.
time_arms <- function(arm_set) {
  kinds <- plant:::census_operating_point_names_tf24()
  out <- list()
  for (nm in names(sites)) for (arm in arm_set) {
    scm <- run_scm(stand_parameters(10), site_env(sites[[nm]], 10),
                   arm_control(arm, cal[[nm]]), run = FALSE)
    el <- system.time(scm$run())[["elapsed"]]
    counts <- colSums(do.call(rbind, plant:::census_operating_point_counts_tf24(scm)))
    names(counts) <- kinds
    out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.frame(site = nm, arm = arm, elapsed = el,
      steps = length(scm$ode_times), t(counts))
  }
  do.call(rbind, out)
}
timing <- rbind(cached("timing_base.rds", time_arms(c("F", "O1", "D"))),
                cached("timing_cal.rds", time_arms(c("Oc", "Ol", "L"))))
kind_cols <- setdiff(names(timing), c("site", "arm", "elapsed", "steps"))
timing$solves <- rowSums(timing[kind_cols])
tt <- timing |> mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arms_all)) |> arrange(site, arm) |>
  group_by(site) |>
  mutate(`× time of Oc` = elapsed / elapsed[arm == "Oc"],
         `µs per solve` = 1e6 * elapsed / solves) |> ungroup()
knitr::kable(tt[c("site", "arm", "elapsed", "steps", "solves", "× time of Oc", "µs per solve")],
             digits = c(0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 1, 1), big.mark = ",",
             col.names = c("Site", "Arm", "Seconds", "ODE steps", "Leaf solves", "× time of Oc", "µs per solve"),
             caption = "One plain run_scm() per arm, 10-year stand, no census.")
```

## Fifty-year patches and fitness

The same stands run for 50 years, now as plant's standard meta-population patch (patches disturbed at random, with fitness the lifetime offspring of a seed averaged over patch age). The cohort grid is quarterly. O1 is left out; its 10-year behaviour is F's.

At the arid site no cohort reaches reproductive size within 50 years, so every arm's fitness there is of order 10⁻¹⁴ and its relative differences carry no information. Fitness is compared at the temperate site only.

```{r runs50}
arms50 <- cached("arms50.rds", lapply(sites, function(site) {
  cl <- cal[[site$name]]
  sapply(arms_plot, function(a)
    run_arm(site, a, cl, years = 50, census_dt = 1 / 4,
            patch_type = "meta-population"), simplify = FALSE)
}))
series50 <- series_of(arms50, arms_plot)
sizes50 <- sizes_of(arms50, arms_plot, c(10, 25, 50))
```

```{r fig-stand50}
#| fig-height: 7.5
#| fig-cap: "Fifty-year trajectories, meta-population patch. Where D (black) cannot be seen, L lies on top of it."
plot_stand(series50)
```

```{r fig-sizes50}
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-cap: "Plants per m² at least a given height, at years 10, 25 and 50."
plot_sizes(sizes50, c(10, 25, 50))
```

```{r table50}
fit50 <- bind_rows(lapply(names(arms50), function(nm)
  bind_rows(lapply(arms_plot, function(a) {
    r <- arms50[[nm]][[a]]
    data.frame(site = nm, arm = a, fitness = r$fitness[[1]], seconds = r$elapsed)
  }))))
rel50 <- outcome_table(series50, sizes50, 50, fit50 |> select(site, arm, fitness))
rel50 |>
  left_join(fit50 |> select(site, arm, seconds), by = c("site", "arm")) |>
  transmute(Site = site, Arm = arm, `Fitness (net reproduction)` = pct(fitness),
            `LAI` = pct(leaf_area), `Above-ground mass` = pct(mass_above_ground),
            `Cumulative uptake` = pct(uptake), `Tallest cohort` = pct(top_height),
            `Worst LAI, yr 1-50` = pct(max_lai_dev)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Difference from D at year 50.")
fit50 |> mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arms_plot), fitness = signif(fitness, 3)) |>
  arrange(site, arm) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 20, 0), format.args = list(scientific = -2), col.names = c("Site", "Arm", "Net reproduction ratio", "Seconds (with census)"),
               caption = "Resident fitness and run time, 50-year meta-population patch.")
```

## Next

- **Invader fitness landscapes**: does each method put the fitness peak for a trait (lma, stem P50) where D does? Mutant runs replay the resident's field, so this costs D its resident run plus a mutant run per trait value.
- **Real sites**: Isaac's flux-tower drivers enter as the same three drivers (noon SWdown, noon VPD, relative VPD amplitude), but warm sites will push VPD past what the 25 °C leaf-temperature pin allows.
